options: evaporation of sweat transfers heat from the skin
questions.a: B) evaporation of sweat transfers heat from the skin. Water evaporating from the skin takes thermal energy with it.

questions.q: When cold, blood vessels to the skin...
Big question: how does your body keep its temperature near 37 °C?
questions.a: Sweating and vasodilation lose heat when hot; vasoconstriction and shivering keep heat when cold.

questions.model: One clear sentence with the key idea: keeping internal conditions (such as temperature and water content) constant.

questions.q: Name two excretory products of the skin.
questions.a: Water and urea (and salts) in sweat.

questions.q: Explain why shivering warms the body.
questions.a: Muscles contract rapidly (1), respiration increases releasing heat (1).

questions.q: Describe how the body responds when its temperature rises above 37 °C. Portal response box.
questions.a: Change detected by receptors/brain (1); sweat glands produce more sweat (1); evaporation transfers heat (1); arterioles to skin dilate (1); more blood near surface (1); more heat lost by radiation (1).
questions.model: Teacher starts: 'The rise in temperature is detected by the brain. Sweat glands in the skin release more sweat...'

questions.q: Compare the speed and duration of nervous and hormonal responses using adrenaline as an example.
questions.a: Nervous responses are faster but short-lived (1); adrenaline travels in the blood, acts more slowly but lasts longer (1).

questions.q: After a meal, blood glucose rises. Describe the role of insulin.
questions.a: Pancreas detects the rise (1) and releases insulin into the blood (1); insulin causes glucose to be taken up by cells and stored (as glycogen in the liver), lowering blood glucose (1).
